summary: A Poison Control article on tea tree oil, a natural essential oil from the Australian tree Melaleuca alternifolia long used for skin ailments. Some evidence supports its use on certain skin conditions, but it is poisonous if swallowed and can irritate skin and harm pets. The article reviews traditional uses, studies, side effects, poisoning cases and prevention tips.
one_line: Poison Control explains that tea tree oil may help some skin conditions but is poisonous if swallowed and risky for pets.
key_facts: Tea tree oil comes from the leaves of an Australian tree called Melaleuca alternifolia.
In 2011, Poison Control received nearly twice as many calls about tea tree oil as about any other named essential oil, including cinnamon, clove and eucalyptus oil.
More than 10 percent of people exposed to tea tree oil were treated in a hospital or doctor's office.
A 1994 study found tea tree oil and the antifungal drug clotrimazole had approximately the same effect on fingernail fungus.
A 1990 study found tea tree oil and benzoyl peroxide were both effective for acne; tea tree oil worked more slowly but caused fewer side effects.
A 1992 study found tea tree oil was no better than placebo at curing fungus infection, though it improved symptoms as much as tolnaftate.
Studies do not support the idea that tea tree oil boosts the immune system.
A child who swallowed a small amount of tea tree oil by mistake went into a coma but recovered.
Large amounts of tea tree oil applied to cats and dogs caused tremors, weakness, difficulty walking, low body temperature and excessive salivation.
Swallowed tea tree oil can cause dangerous poisoning in less than thirty minutes; call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.
In one case an elderly man swallowed a teaspoon and developed dizziness, vomiting and slurred speech, but recovered at home.
In another case a middle-aged woman used tea tree oil and 3% hydrogen peroxide as an enema, per online advice, and presented with bloody diarrhea needing IV fluids and pain medication.
A single report linked products containing lavender oil and tea tree oil to breast enlargement in a young boy.
